messages.content: Took it out yesterday for about 3h on the road - rural/curvy and interstate highway.   Overall well-balanced.  Good torque in low-speed turns.   I go by how much I want to nudge the wheel or need to otherwise intervene, and there was as little of that as any other model.   Chill long with DEM on, I barely noticed it flipping back and forth.  New daily driver.
How does this compare to gwm9 for you people
I prefer GWM9 still. The lateral on this model hugs just a little to close to the apex of the corners where it hits the lane bumps for me.

Bit of an inside curve hugger, agreed.  Long is finally improving though - been getting about 50% successful stop-and-holds at red lights vs. almost zero on previous models.    I.e. lat is not the absolute best yet it's very good, and (experimental) long might be the best so far.    I've been able to stay in experimental mode for relatively long periods of time, a first in OP.    It usually takes off a little slow/slow to reach speed, though once it took off faster than chill.  Will continue to test and would like to see more refinements of this series.

I also took it on a long, one way, winding gravel road @ 10 mph through a nature preserve, and it did very well - exp. long included.  Only thing was it mostly preferred the left side of this (laneless) road.

Take that back on the red lights.   I wonder if it's my car or something... it'll come down to 0 mph, *almost* stopped then creep for a second or two, then try to take off.   Could be related to the previous speed - mine were all stops from ~45 mph.    It did super with a difficult curvy left turn/light though - stopped nicely, made the turn on the green hands off.
I liked lat on this model a lot with my '21 Civic. It followed some curves better than any other model I've tried so far, includng gWM9 and coolGWM. I think this is my new daily
This seems more efficient to me
